main_text.p: » neret: Excitemus igitur fidem;& invocemus » filium Dei, fervantem oves suas: quia simul di- » cit; Audiunt me, & sequuntur me.

Fruftra igitur adversum nos adducitur Melanchthon, recte ex ipsomet & expositus & intellectus. Ita certe eum intellexit fidissimus ejus [illegible, ~8 letters] & μάχος[?], D. Lutherus, in Lib. de servo arbitrio contra Remonstrantium patriarcham & ducem, Erasmum; opponens hujus libello, Locos Theologicos Philippi. Verba sunt in exordio, morae responsionis excusatorio: Supervacaneum videtur, respondere istis argumentis tuis, antea a me quoque toties refutatis; concultatis vero, & protritis prorsus, per Philippi Melanchthonis, de locis Theologicis, invictam libellum, meo judicio, non solum immortalitate; sed canone quoque Ecclesiastico dignum: cui tuus libellus comparatus, ita mihi sordet ac viluit; ut tibi vehementer comparer, qui pulcherrimam tuam & ingeniosam dictionem istis sordibus pollueres.

page.notes: The marginal note beside the Lutherus paragraph is printed in small italic and reads "D. Luther, optimus in-terpres Melanchthonis." Two Greek words in the main text are uncertain: the first after "ejus" is not legible on the scan, and "μάχος" and "ἀμοιβαίοις" are doubtful readings. The » marks at the start of lines are printed quotation marks, and the italic setting is taken from the scan.
